about: The Gospel for the Vigil of the Ascension. Jesus raises His eyes to heaven, asks the Father to glorify Him, and prays for the people entrusted to Him. The reading ends with His coming to the Father.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus lifted His eyes to heaven and said: Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, so that Your Son may glorify You,

ex.w004: Jesus raises His eyes toward heaven before addressing the Father. The English phrase recasts the Latin construction without changing who acts.

nt.w011: Venit can be present or perfect. The context supports the hour having arrived. “Is coming” remains formally possible.

seg.tr: just as You have given Him authority over all humanity, so that He may give eternal life to all whom You have given Him.

ex.w028: The Latin collective “all” refers to the people entrusted to the Son. The later “to them” resumes those same recipients. English already expresses them as “to all.”
ex.w033: This pronoun resumes the people named collectively earlier. English “to all whom…” carries that recipient without repeating “to them.”

nt.w028: Omne can be nominative or accusative. It may stand as a topic resumed by “to them.” Attraction to the relative clause’s accusative remains possible. The referent is people, not an inanimate gift.

seg.tr: Now this is eternal life: for them to know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.

a.g: Jesus Christ, whom You have sent

ex.w048: The one sent by the Father is Jesus Christ. Knowing Him and knowing the Father are the two coordinated objects in the description of eternal life.

seg.tr: I have glorified You on earth; I have completed the work You gave Me to do.
And now, Father, glorify Me Yourself in Your own presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

a.g: I had with You before the world existed

ex.w071: Jesus asks the Father for glory in the Father’s own presence, not in the presence of a third person.
ex.w074: Jesus had this glory with the Father before the world existed. The final “with You” belongs with “I had,” despite its delayed position after the clause about the world.
ex.w078: This phrase identifies with whom Jesus had glory. It does not locate the world’s existence “with You.”

seg.tr: I have made Your name known to the people You gave Me from the world. They were Yours, and You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.

ex.w089: The people belonged to the Father, who gave them to Jesus.

seg.tr: They have now recognized that everything You have given Me is from You,
because I have given them the words You gave Me, and they themselves have received them; they have truly recognized that I came forth from You, and they have believed that You sent Me.

ex.w109: Jesus explains why the disciples recognized the source of His gifts: they received the Father’s words through Him.

seg.tr: I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those You have given Me, because they are Yours.

a.g: I do not pray for the world

ex.w136: The contrast concerns this prayer for the people entrusted to Jesus. It does not say that He never prays for others.

seg.tr: And all that is Mine is Yours, and what is Yours is Mine, and I have been glorified in them.

ex.w159: Jesus describes a completed glorification in these people. The two Latin words form one perfect-passive expression in English.

seg.tr: And I am no longer in the world, and they are in the world, and I am coming to You.

ex.w166: Jesus speaks of His impending departure as a present reality. This does not turn His words into a narration after the Ascension.
